what_its_for: Mepolizumab is a medication used to help control severe asthma in adults and children (6 years and older) when other asthma medicines have not worked well enough. It is also used to treat certain other conditions involving too many white blood cells called eosinophils, such as eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES), and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). It works by blocking a protein in your body that causes these eosinophil cells to build up and cause inflammation.
how_to_take: Mepolizumab is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your upper arm, thigh, or abdomen (belly). It can be given by a healthcare provider in a clinic, or you may be able to inject it yourself at home after proper training. If you are giving it at home, carefully follow the instructions that come with your auto-injector or prefilled syringe. Do not shake the medication. Rotate injection sites each time to avoid soreness. Do not inject into skin that is bruised, red, sore, or hard.
dosing: The usual adult dose for severe asthma is 100 mg given once every 4 weeks. For EGPA, the dose is 300 mg every 4 weeks. For HES, the dose is 300 mg every 4 weeks. For CRSwNP, the dose is 100 mg every 4 weeks. Dosing for children may be different and will be determined by your doctor based on your child's weight and condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or healthcare provider as soon as possible to reschedule your injection. After getting the missed dose, your next dose should be scheduled 4 weeks from that date. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one. Try to stick to your regular schedule to get the best results from this medication.
storage: Store mepolizumab in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. Do not shake the medication. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 86°F or 30°C) for up to 7 days, but then it must be used or thrown away. Keep this medication out of reach of children. Dispose of used syringes and auto-injectors in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Do not stop taking your other asthma or steroid medications unless your doctor tells you to, even if you start feeling better. Stopping steroids too quickly can cause serious problems. Avoid getting live vaccines (such as the nasal flu vaccine) while using this medication without checking with your doctor first. Tell your doctor if you have or think you have a parasitic (worm) infection before starting this medicine, as it may make it harder for your body to fight certain infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as: hives, rash, itching, swelling of your face, mouth, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness, or feeling faint. These reactions can happen within hours or even days after your injection. Also contact your doctor if you have: fever, chills, or signs of infection; worsening breathing problems or asthma attacks; joint or back pain; or any other new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Mepolizumab does not work immediately. Most people begin to notice improvements in their asthma symptoms, such as fewer attacks and better breathing, within a few weeks to months of starting treatment. It may take up to 6 months to see the full benefit. Continue using it as directed even if you do not notice changes right away. This medication helps prevent symptoms over time, so it is important to keep your scheduled injections.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. There is limited information about the safety of mepolizumab during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before using this medication. Children: Mepolizumab is approved for children aged 6 and older for severe asthma, and for children 12 and older for certain other conditions. The dose may be different for children depending on their weight. Older adults: No dose adjustment is generally needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Parasitic infections: If you live in or travel to areas where parasitic worm infections are common, tell your doctor before starting this medication.
